transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05   Start: 16:00 PDT   Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM); Ruth Park (Acadia Head of Security), Devon Malik (Platform Eng), Sanjay Rao (CTO), Ana Gomez (Compliance)

Auto Summary (auto-generated):
- Quick review of last week's test results: audit logs captured, retention pipeline working but redaction gaps noted.
- SSO progress: SAML assertion mapping mostly done; one attribute mismatch for employee_id.
- Action items: Redwood to provide redacted audit sample and forwarding guide; Acadia to confirm retention window and share allowlist for VPC peering.

Topics: SSO/SAML, Audit log shape and shipping, Retention & redaction, SOC2 evidence for pilot, RBAC/KMS notes.

Action items (captured above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: OK, hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, we got Liam and Priya on from our side. How's everyone?
[00:18] Ruth: Hi Maya, hi team. We're good, been reviewing the logs you sent last night. A few things to go over on retention and what we can actually ship to our bench- uh, to audit team.
[00:30] Liam: Great, yeah so quick agenda - SSO status, audit log example, retention policy gap we discovered, and then SOC2 artifacts for the pilot.
[00:42] Devon: Sounds good. On SSO our engineers hit one mapping problem, the employee id is coming across as "empId" in the assertion but our user directory expects "employee_id", small mapping mismatch.
[00:56] Maya: Got it, that should be just a SAML attribute map tweak on your IdP. Liam, can you call out the recommended claim map?
[01:05] Liam: Sure-- I put the mapping in the playbook doc but to repeat quickly: map empId -> employee_id, include groups claim as 'roles', and include eduPersonAffiliation if you use it. Also, note our SAML library currently treats RelayState a little differently, sometimes the console doesn't auto-redirect if RelayState is blank.
[01:30] Ruth: Hmm we did see a redirect loop once, that might be the RelayState thing.
[01:36] Priya: We'll add a troubleshooting note in the doc.
[01:40] Ana: Quick question - for SOC2 evidence, can we get proof of SSO login events into the audit logs?
[01:48] Liam: Yes, we emit auth events as part of the platform audit stream - login success/failure, token issuance, session expiry - all as structured JSON. I'll attach a sample, redacted.
[01:59] Sanjay: When you say audit stream, is that sent to our SIEM or is it in Red wood's console only?
[02:07] Maya: Two options - you can forward via HTTPS webhook to your SIEM, or we can set up syslog/forwarders to your collector in the VPC. For Dedicated/on-prem we typically do direct forwarding. For hosted API it's webhook or S3 delivery.
[02:27] Devon: For the pilot we'd prefer direct forward into our Splunk instance inside the VPC. What's the auth mechanism there?
[02:35] Liam: We support TLS mutual auth for log forwarding, and API-key + TLS as fallback. For VPC peering option we'll open an egress path to your collector and use mTLS with client certs.
[02:47] Ruth: OK that's ideal. Do you include raw prompts or model outputs in the audit payload? That is critical for us.
[02:56] Liam: Important nuance - by default the audit payload includes metadata (request id, model id, timestamps, user id, token counts) and a hashed or redacted preview of inputs. We don't sink full PII or full prompt text unless you explicitly enable full payload capture in the config. For pilot we've been shipping with preview-only.
[03:15] Ana: Is the redaction deterministic? Our legal wants to ensure we can reproduce an audit trail that ties to a request without exposing PII.
[03:23] Liam: We use a reversible tokenization option for enterprise customers with KMS integration - basically we encrypt the full prompt and store the encrypted blob; the audit record contains a pointer and a deterministic HMAC that ties to the request id. That way you can request decryption under a strict access control flow.
[03:40] Ruth: That sounds OK but we need to see KMS integration docs and the role-based access controls that gate decryption.
[03:48] Maya: We'll include KMS flow diagrams in the package. Liam can share the RBAC policy template.
[03:55] Liam: Yep. Also one caveat: if you use the hosted plan and don't bring your own KMS, the key is managed by Redwood by default; for compliance you can bring your own key (BYOK) or HSM integration.
[04:10] Sanjay: For this pilot we need BYOK. We're not comfortable with a Redwood-managed key for test data.
[04:16] Maya: Totally understood, we'll include BYOK steps in the onboarding doc.
[04:22] Devon: Switching to retention - we ran the retention job against the test corpus and found that certain system-generated traces were not being redacted. Specifically, user emails in the metadata field remained.
[04:33] Liam: Right, that was one of the gaps we flagged. The retention engine has a rule-set you can customize - regex-based redaction plus PII classifiers. We shipped a default conservative set but it missed a nested metadata field that was vendor-specific.
[04:49] Ruth: Can the classifier be tuned to your corpus? We have a lot of vendor-specific email patterns and internal ticket numbers.
[04:57] Liam: Yes, you can register custom patterns and training examples. For the pilot we can push a custom rule pack. I'll need a sample (redacted) to tune our classifier.
[05:06] Ana: We'll provide a small sample of ten problem records. Is that enough?
[05:11] Liam: That's a good start. Also note we support a 'safe-sample' mode where we keep raw text encrypted and only expose redacted view; retention enforcement still deletes the encrypted blob after the retention period.
[05:24] Maya: Operational question from my side - what retention window are you trying to validate in the pilot?
[05:29] Ruth: We're proposing 90 days for search traces and 365 for system logs, but legal wants to double-check with data governance.
[05:37] Sanjay: 90-day is our desired setting for generated content, we can keep system telemetry longer.
[05:42] Maya: OK we'll test the 90-day policy for prompt/response artifacts and 365 for platform telemetry. We'll also simulate deletion to show evidence.
[05:51] Devon: About SOC2 - what artifacts can you give us during pilot to show control operation?
[05:57] Priya: We can provide operational runbooks, evidence of access reviews (redacted), change logs, and the audit stream we've discussed. Full SOC2 report is available for enterprise accounts; for pilot we can provide assertion documents and our security whitepaper.
[06:11] Ana: Are there periodic access reviews included? We need to see a sample of monthly access recertification.
[06:18] Liam: Yes, we have an access recert process. I'll pull a redacted sample audit that shows access revocations and group changes.
[06:25] Ruth: Also, for RBAC - we need fine grained roles in the console. Can a junior ops person see only metrics and not be able to pull logs?
[06:34] Liam: Yep, RBAC supports role templates: Viewer, Auditor, Admin, DevOps. Auditor can't download raw prompts; DevOps can. You can customize roles via API or Console.
[06:45] Sanjay: One more question on fallback: if a Dedicated node is overloaded do you fail over to a hosted variant? We want predictable behavior for compliance.
[06:54] Maya: We support routed fallback per policy. For compliance-sensitive workloads you can disable cross-tenant fallback. For your Dedicated pilot we'll show a policy that keeps data in VPC only and fails requests rather than routing to hosted.
[07:06] Ruth: Good. We also need to ensure audit logs are immutable once written - can they be tampered with?
[07:12] Liam: We sign logs with an append-only digest chain and optionally ship to an external WORM store (S3 with Object Lock) for long term retention. That gives immutability guarantees.
[07:23] Devon: Regarding network - we will provide IP allowlist and internal CIDR. How long does it take to set up VPC peering on your side?
[07:31] Maya: For Dedicated it's typically 2-3 business days after we get the peering config and certs. For the pilot we can do a pre-setup to speed it.
[07:40] Ana: Are there any known gaps that would block us from classifying this pilot as SOC2-ready?
[07:46] Priya: Nothing blocking; most items are documentation, KMS BYOK steps, and the retention tuning we discussed. The redaction gaps are the main technical issue but remediable.
[07:58] Ruth: OK sounds fair. We'll need the remediation evidence in two weeks to present to our auditors.
[08:05] Maya: We'll prioritize the redaction patch and the audit sample. Liam, estimate ETA?
[08:10] Liam: I can produce a tuned rule pack and redacted sample in 5 business days, plus KMS docs in the same window. So target Oct 12.
[08:19] Sanjay: We'll aim to review by Oct 15. If all good, we'll move to the on-prem connectivity test week of Oct 18.
[08:27] Ruth: Are there any cost implications for enabling BYOK and mTLS log forwarding?
[08:33] Maya: BYOK doesn't carry an extra fee aside from integration effort; mTLS forwarding has a small egress/data-transfer estimate for Dedicated — we'll add the numbers in the updated SOW.
[08:44] Devon: One small note — in the runtime logs we noticed the "KV cache" reference appears sometimes as "K V cache" in the JSON key, which broke a parsing job on our side. Can you normalize?
[08:55] Liam: Yeah, we've seen that in older kernel skus where the tokenization injector added spaces. We'll include a normalization step in the export pipeline so key names are stable.
[09:08] Ana: For the evidence package, can you also include an example of the deletion event showing the lifecycle of a request from create -> redact -> delete?
[09:16] Liam: Absolutely, I'll include a sample timeline and the corresponding signed log entries.
[09:23] Maya: OK big picture recap before we wrap. We will: 1) Provide redacted audit sample + forwarding guide (Liam) by Oct 12; 2) Provide BYOK/KMS integration docs and RBAC templates (Maya/Liam) by Oct 12; 3) Acadia to confirm retention windows and provide sample records (Ruth/Devon) by Oct 15; 4) Schedule VPC peering test week of Oct 18 (Priya to coordinate).
[09:46] Ruth: That matches our notes. Anything else?
[09:50] Sanjay: Just one ask - include a short runbook for incident response for exposure of PII during the pilot.
[09:56] Priya: We'll include an incident response playbook as part of the evidence pack.
[10:01] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send the updated SOW and the doc pack after this call.
[10:06] Devon: Thanks, bye.
[10:10] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: a few product names auto-transcribed differently (e.g., "Red wood" instead of "Redwood", "cannery" for "canary") and occasional mis-placed spaces in codes/keys.
